_doc: Which TIER of the layered level badge the player sees, by Level. The badge is composited from cut parts in games/grove/assets/ui/lvl_parts/ (see Kit.level_badge); a tier decomposes group=tier/6, stage=tier%6+1. The Level->tier map is BANDED so it advances fast early and slows down: walk `bands` in order, each contributes `tiers` consecutive tier indices that each span `levels_per_tier` levels. Past the last band the tier holds at tier_count-1. The legacy single-band form (top-level levels_per_tier, no bands) is still honoured. Banding: L1-10 one tier per level, L11-40 every 3 levels, L41-100 every 6 levels = 30 tiers.

medal._doc: The HUD's top-left paper MEDAL badge (Look.make_star_level_badge) — a THREE-tier family, and the only place its Level->tier thresholds live. THE THRESHOLDS ARE DERIVED FROM `bands` ABOVE, not invented: that ladder is three bands of ten tiers, so the medal wears one tier per BAND and its joints are the ladder's own — L1-10 (band 1, one tier per level), L11-40 (band 2, every 3 levels), L41+ (band 3 and beyond). The approved mocks were labelled Lv2 / Lv24 / Lv85, which are ladder tiers 1 / 14 / 27 — the 1st, 2nd and 3rd band, matching. RETUNE HERE: `min_level` is the first Level that wears each medal, and engine/tests/level_badge_medal_tests.gd asserts these still equal the band starts, so a deliberate retune fails loudly instead of silently drifting from the ladder. `circle_cy` is the DISC's centre as a fraction of the texture canvas height (measured with the widest-row rule on the shipped 256 bake — the number rides the disc, not the art's bbox, which t1's tails, t2's ribbon and t3's banner all pull off centre). `painted_span` is the painted art's height as a fraction of that canvas, so the badge's px slot sizes the medal and not its transparent gutter.
